name: AI Deep Dive — KRMN — 2026-05-31
rationale: Karman Holdings manufactures the physical structural and propulsion components that go inside hypersonic missiles, strategic defense systems, and space launch vehicles — precisely the hardware the Pentagon is replenishing and expanding at record rates. The fundamentals are genuinely improving: gross margins have expanded every single year (35.8%→40.3%), the company is becoming profitable, and revenue nearly doubles to $730M in 2026E (+55%). The low trailing net margin (3.7%) is artificially depressed by PE-era leverage; the 2026 EPS jump from $0.13→$0.57 reflects debt paydown normalizing net income toward the 15% operating margin. The DCF yields a conservative $18.05 weighted fair value using standard Industrials exit multiples (16-35x P/E), implying 69% downside from $57.50. However, 10 analysts have a consensus target of $105.60 (BUY), reflecting a growth-premium valuation framework that assigns 40-50x exit P/E to a company growing EPS 60%+ per year. The tension between these two frameworks reflects the stock's nature: a genuine defense infrastructure compounder re-rated as a high-growth name. After a 38% pullback from recent highs, the risk-reward has improved materially.

Net margin of 5% assumes operating margins settle around 12% (below historical peak of 18.4%) as SG&A for the public company scales and interest expense does not decline as fast as modeled. Exit P/E of 16 is below Industrials conservative benchmark (14 is the floor), reflecting growth disappointment. Quality multiplier 0.95 reflects limited demonstrated moat at this stage — programs are won on competitive bid, not sole-source. Historical bear trough for Industrials net margins is 2%.
risks: Defense budget sequestration or continuing resolution delays contract ramps by 1-2 years
Operating margins compress further (TTM decline from 18.4%→15.5% accelerates) as public company overhead grows

bull.rationale: Bull catalyst: Pentagon missile refresh (aging Minuteman III ICBM fleet + LRSO long-range standoff weapon program + GBSD ground-based strategic deterrent) creates 10+ year demand for Karman's propulsion systems, payload protection structures, and aerodynamic interstage systems. Golden Dome space-based missile defense layer requires 1,000s of interceptors at scale — Karman is a Tier 1 structural/propulsion supplier. 28% CAGR brings revenue to $1.62B (3.4x current). Net margin of 15% achievable with: (a) high-value sole-source classified programs at premium margins, (b) operating leverage on $1.6B revenue base, (c) interest expense fully eliminated. Exit P/E of 35 reflects growth premium — company still growing 18%+ in Y5 with improving margins (PEG ratio at 35x/18% ≈ 1.9x, at the high end but not extreme for defense infrastructure). Quality multiplier 1.10 reflects one specific moat: once Karman's structural components are spec'd into a DoD weapons program (e.g., GBSD interstage), switching costs for a production-phase program are extremely high (re-certification, testing, schedule risk).
risks: Defense budget reprioritization reduces hypersonics and missile refresh spending in late program years
Re-rating compression if EPS growth slows below 30% before Y5, compressing the 35x terminal multiple

aiThesis.rationale: Karman Holdings makes the physical structural backbone of modern missiles and rockets: payload fairings, interstage structures, propulsion systems for hypersonics, and aerodynamic assemblies. This is not a narrative play — it is actual hardware inside weapons programs that the Pentagon is funding at record levels. The business is genuinely improving: gross margins expanded from 35.8% to 40.3% over four years, EPS is set to quadruple in 2026 as PE-era debt clears post-IPO, and the company's revenue is on track to double in a single year. The DCF fair value of $18.05 uses standard Industrials exit multiples (16-35x P/E) and produces a technical SELL signal at $57.50. However, this understates the company's value as a high-growth defense infrastructure compounder: 10 analysts target $105.60 using growth-company multiples (40-80x forward P/E) that reflect the EPS CAGR of 60%+ expected through 2027. The critical reconciliation: to justify $57.50 on a 5-year DCF requires roughly 30% CAGR and 15%+ net margins at a 40x terminal P/E — achievable if Pentagon missile refresh programs reach full ramp. At $57.50 (down 38% from recent highs), the stock has already priced out significant optimism. The bear case ($2.86) is severe but requires both growth disappointment AND margin failure simultaneously. SELL per DCF formula, but this is a growth premium business where standard Industrials benchmarks systematically understate value. Would HOLD for investors with conviction on the Pentagon spending thesis.
